articles.title: Sparkle Galaxy
articles.summary: Dense galaxy-cluster sparkle with bright concentrated zones and dark voids; matte base with medium metallic flake, in whatever colour you give it. Reads as a matte colour with one lighter sparkling river across it; the dust is fine enough to look like a soft milky glow.
articles.what: Dense galaxy-cluster sparkle distribution with concentrated bright zones and dark voids Up close: Takes your colour (the purple shown is only a placeholder). Over a lightly speckled matte field runs one wide S-shaped band, about 80-100 px across, thick with bright fine sparkle dust like the Milky Way; outside the band the sparkle is sparse and dim. From a distance: Reads as a matte colour with one lighter sparkling river across it; the dust is fine enough to look like a soft milky glow. Measured spec (average): metal 98, roughness 194, coat 82. Shine: matte. Metal: medium. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Sparkle Galaxy" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Sides and hood: the S-band sweeps across a wide panel
Single band per tile, so on a long thin panel it may be cut off or repeated
White or black numbers read; numbers crossing the band lose a little contrast to the dust.
Large bold shapes (stripes, big graphics, numbers): the band stays behind them
Pairs well with: black, deep blue, purple, chrome.
pitfalls: Not an even all-over glitter: it is one wide curving band over sparse dust
Not a bold flake: the sparkle is fine dust
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other sparkle finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 98 (pearl-level metal), roughness 194 (matte or blasted), clearcoat 82 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other sparkle finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: large bold shapes (stripes, big graphics, numbers): the band stays behind them; soft fades or clouds in a darker tone: add a nebula feel
Patterns to avoid: fine glitter, speckle or static patterns: noise on noise; stripes along the same band: fight it
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat sheen: makes the dust pop; none needed
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Sparkle Lightning Bug
articles.summary: Bioluminescent glow points scattered on a dark base, like lightning bug flicker; semi-matte with medium metallic flake, in whatever colour you give it. Reads as a base colour with a glowing lime-green speckle over it, like fireflies in a field; the dots merge to a soft green-lit shimmer.
articles.what: Green-tinted bioluminescent glow points on dark base — warm summer lightning bug flicker Up close: Soft round glow dots about 8-14 px wide in lime-yellow-green, randomly scattered and dense enough to overlap into a cloudy field over a fine speckled base. Edges are fuzzy like lit-up bokeh, not hard flakes. From a distance: Reads as a base colour with a glowing lime-green speckle over it, like fireflies in a field; the dots merge to a soft green-lit shimmer. Measured spec (average): metal 131, roughness 153, coat 112. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: medium. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, show car, truck / off-road.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Sparkle Lightning Bug" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: wide panels show the spread of glow dots
Dark base paint gives the best effect
Dots are soft and low contrast: numbers read fine in white or black; avoid lime green numbers.
None or a dark fade: a dark base makes the glow dots read as fireflies
Pairs well with: black, deep green, chrome, white.
pitfalls: Not hard glitter flake: the dots are soft round glows
Not a fixed colour: the base takes the colour you give it (render uses neutral grey input), only the glow tint is green
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other sparkle finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 131 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 153 (semi-matte), clearcoat 112 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to other sparkle finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: none or a dark fade: a dark base makes the glow dots read as fireflies; a thin pinstripe: stays out of the way
Patterns to avoid: other flake and glitter patterns: bury the glow dots; busy camo: muddy
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear: makes the glow dots pop like wet lights; dull clear: keeps a dusty night feel
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Sparkle Meteor
articles.summary: Warm orange-brown sparkle with fine streaked bright points all running one direction, like a meteor trail; matte, low metal. Reads as a matte colour with a fine warm sandy shimmer and a faint diagonal grain; the dashes blur into a directional brushed-glitter feel.
articles.what: Directional meteor trail sparkle with streaked bright points all moving in one direction Up close: Matte surface with a faint cloudy mottle, covered in tiny bright dashes 4-8 px long, all slanting the same way from upper-left to lower-right like falling streaks of rain or meteor trails. The dashes are peach-orange and sit in loose clusters. From a distance: Reads as a matte colour with a fine warm sandy shimmer and a faint diagonal grain; the dashes blur into a directional brushed-glitter feel. Measured spec (average): metal 80, roughness 211, coat 75. Shine: matte. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Sparkle Meteor" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: panels where the streak direction follows the airflow look best
Whole body: consistent direction keeps it tidy
Fine and low contrast: numbers stay clear in white or black.
Stripes running along the dash direction: reinforce the motion
Pairs well with: in whatever colour you give it, bronze, black, cream.
pitfalls: Not even round glitter: every dash leans the same way
Not brushed metal: the dashes are separate points, not continuous lines
Avoid: stripes running against the streak direction, gloss clear kills the matte trail.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 80 (pearl-level metal), roughness 211 (flat), clearcoat 75 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: stripes running against the streak direction, gloss clear kills the matte trail.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: stripes running along the dash direction: reinforce the motion; a plain fade: calm contrast to the fine grain
Patterns to avoid: stripes across the dash direction: fight the flow; gloss clear: kills the matte dust look
Spec overlays that work: dull clear: keeps the matte meteor dust; fine micro-flake: slightly more points
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Sparkle Snowfall
articles.summary: Dense cold pale sparkle field, icy white points on a frozen light base; matte, fine, looks like fresh snow in sun. Reads as a matte colour with a faint frosted, slightly icy shimmer; the glints are too fine to see as dots.
articles.what: Dense cold crystal sparkle field with icy white points on pale frozen base — fresh snow Up close: Takes your colour (the grey shown is the neutral input). Over it lies a fine frosted grain with tiny cold white and ice-blue glints, 1-3 px, evenly scattered like sugar or crushed ice. Subtle at 1:1, the grain only shows up when zoomed. From a distance: Reads as a matte colour with a faint frosted, slightly icy shimmer; the glints are too fine to see as dots. Measured spec (average): metal 79, roughness 198, coat 90. Shine: matte. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Sparkle Snowfall" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, sides: broad panels where the shimmer shows
All-over field, no seam visible
Any contrasting numbers read perfectly; the grain barely touches their edges.
Large bold shapes (stripes, big graphics, numbers): the frost stays quiet behind them
Pairs well with: in whatever colour you give it, ice blue, white, silver.
pitfalls: Not visible snowflakes or big dots: the glints are tiny
Not chrome or mirror: matte and low metal
Avoid: dark numbers disappear on pale base, warm colours clash with the cold look.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 79 (pearl-level metal), roughness 198 (matte or blasted), clearcoat 90 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: dark numbers disappear on pale base, warm colours clash with the cold look.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: large bold shapes (stripes, big graphics, numbers): the frost stays quiet behind them; soft fades or clouds: add a winter feel
Patterns to avoid: fine glitter, speckle or static patterns: pile into noise; other flake finishes
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat sheen: makes the glints pop; none needed: it is quiet already
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Sparkle Starfield
articles.summary: User-colored fine starfield material: pale grain and tiny bright pinpoints over the chosen base; matte, medium metal, subtle sparkle. Reads as a plain matte colour; the stars cannot be seen at distance and only a slight cloudy dust remains.
articles.what: Sparse bright star-point sparkles on deep dark base — night sky with scattered pinpricks Up close: Takes your colour (the grey-blue shown is the neutral input). A very fine pale grain with soft cloudy variation about 30 px across, and only a handful of tiny bright pinpoints at 2x. At 1:1 it looks like a smooth matte colour with a faint dusty mottle. From a distance: Reads as a plain matte colour; the stars cannot be seen at distance and only a slight cloudy dust remains. Measured spec (average): metal 104, roughness 221, coat 94. Shine: matte. Metal: medium. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Sparkle Starfield" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, sides: broad panels let the dust show in sun
All-over field, no seam visible
Any contrasting numbers read perfectly; the grain does not touch edges.
Large bold shapes (stripes, big graphics, numbers): the dust stays quiet behind them
Pairs well with: deep navy, black, silver trim, matte clear.
pitfalls: Not visible stars at 1:1: the pinpoints are rare and tiny
Not much different from Sparkle Snowfall in the render: both are a fine pale grain on a matte colour; this one is rougher and has fewer glints
Avoid: pale base hides stars, busy under numbers.
